note: Every model Doctine runs or is evaluating, what it is for, who owns what, and what it is allowed to do. tests/ai-registry.test.mjs fails if the server can route to a model that isn't listed here. Status words: deployed (in use by real people), configured_off (in the code, switched off or without a key), candidate (being evaluated), proposed (not built). No entry may be called Doctine-trained unless Doctine trained its weights.

models.location: public/index.html parseText, runs on the person's device
limitations: Misses about 3 in 10 rows on photographed (OCR) reports.
Leaves out decimal-comma values and tells the person (by design).

models.ownership: third-party hosted model (Anthropic); Doctine owns the prompts, schemas, routing and validation around it
models.location: Anthropic API, called only from the server with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
models.evaluation: not run: no API key in any environment (gate 6 fails on staging for this reason)
limitations: Sends document images and text to Anthropic when switched on; needs the provider-terms review in DOCTINE_CLINICAL_SAFETY_AND_COMPLIANCE.md before real patient data.
Used only for short explanations of conflict-free results.
Highest cost; only for conflicts, unit changes and long histories.

models.ownership: would be Doctine-trained LoRA adapter weights on an open-weight base model (the base model stays third-party)

base_model_shortlist.license: Apache-2.0 (Hugging Face model card, checked 26 Nov 2026)

models.evaluation: must beat b0-app-parser on extraction-v1 test (OCR input) with zero wrong values before any shadow run; training set: ai-lab/train/make_sft.py; run: ai-lab/train/train_lora.py
limitations: Not trained. No claim of a Doctine model may be made until it is.
